purpose: Which numbering Word shows for a paragraph that gets w:numPr from its paragraph style chain, and how a direct w:numPr combines with it (#1244).
procedure: Minimal packages (content types, package and document rels, document.xml, numbering.xml, styles.xml) were opened in Word and each paragraph's `list string of list format` was read through AppleScript; the same packages were converted to PDF with headless LibreOffice and read with `pdftotext -layout`. Paragraph text names the w:num and w:ilvl it uses (e.g. "p3 n4L1").
finding: A paragraph's w:numId and w:ilvl each come from the nearest layer that sets them: the paragraph's own w:numPr first, then the style chain (w:pStyle, following w:basedOn; the default paragraph style when the paragraph names no style or an undefined one, t4, s_e). A missing w:ilvl means level 0. w:numId 0 at the winning layer turns numbering off (s_b, s_e). Word does NOT ignore a style's w:ilvl in favour of the level whose w:pStyle names the style, as ECMA-376 Part 1 17.3.1.19 / 17.9.23 say: it uses the style's w:ilvl (0 when absent), and shows NO number when that level's w:pStyle does not name the nearest style in the paragraph's chain that some level links to (or names a style while no style in the chain is linked): H3NoIlvl, H2IlvlOnly, X0, X2explicit, XNumIdOnlyU, Q1, Q1b, Q1c and QU show nothing, while Heading1, Heading2, MyClause (basedOn Heading2), XU, XIlvlOnlyU and Q0 are numbered. A level w:pStyle link with no w:numPr on the style numbers nothing (s_c). The link check applies to style-derived numbering only: a direct w:numPr naming only w:ilvl or only w:numId merges with a valid style numPr (s_b: 'H2 ilvl2-only direct' shows (a), 'H2 direct numId10 no-ilvl' shows Section 1.03), and a direct w:numPr over an invalid style numbering gets nothing from it ('QU direct ilvl1 only'). Style-numbered and directly numbered paragraphs advance the same shared counters (s_d). LibreOffice 26.2 follows the spec instead: no link check (H3NoIlvl shows ARTICLE II, H2IlvlOnly shows Section 1.03, X0 shows ARTICLE I, XNumIdOnlyU continues the decimal list); safe-docx follows Word. Unrelated to style resolution: in s_b Word shows 'Section 1.02' for the first level-1 paragraph after an (a) at level 2, because Word counts a skipped level as used at its start value; safe-docx renders the skipped-level case separately (follow-up to #1243).
